title: Philadelphia Fed Fourth Quarter 2026 Survey of Professional Forecasters — 10:00 a.m. ET, the oldest quarterly macro consensus in the US and the only one this calendar could quote a CPI/GDP forecast from
source: EST: philadelphiafed.org/calendar-of-events, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 131,096 bytes) — the Philadelphia Fed's own release calendar, whose embedded structured data enumerates the FULL 2026 SPF schedule as four rows, all at 10:00 a.m.: 'First Quarter 2026 Survey of Professional Forecasters | Mar 6', 'Second Quarter | May 15', 'Third Quarter | Aug 14', and verbatim 'Fourth Quarter 2026 Survey of Professional Forecasters | Nov 16 2026 | 10:00 a.m.' The four dates are Fridays or Mondays in the second week of the quarter's middle month, consistent with the SPF's published mid-quarter cadence. Filed estimate on three counts: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no member for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule (FED: covers the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar only), this lane never self-confirms an event it discovered in-sweep, and only the calendar row was read — no SPF-specific release page was fetched. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of philly-fed-price-inflation-expectations-q4-2026-11-25, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED (not canonical) by the philly-fed-price-inflation-expectations-q4-2026-11-25 initial-research adjacency sweep on 2026-09-09, found in the same calendar payload that dated its proposer. Filed because it is the strictly more market-relevant half of a pair this calendar currently tracks neither half of. The SPF is the Philadelphia Fed's quarterly survey of professional macro forecasters — running since 1968, the longest continuously-published US macro consensus — and it is the source FOMC-watchers quote for consensus CPI, core PCE, GDP and unemployment paths, including the 10-year inflation expectation that appears in Fed communications. Its proposer, PIES, is a sub-state survey of Third District FIRMS; this is a national forecaster panel. Corridor case: 2026-11-16 sits two days before fomc-minutes-2026-11-18 (medium, confirmed) and twelve days before fomc-blackout-start-2026-11-28 (medium, confirmed), so it is the last published professional consensus before the December FOMC blackout closes — and it lands the day before retail-sales-2026-11-17 (high, confirmed) rather than on top of it, which is more identification than most of this corridor gets. Impact LOW and symbols [] provisionally, on the same grounds as every other survey entry on this shelf and NOT on measurement: no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is macro-keyed, and no tracked name carries a forecaster-survey channel. Whoever writes the canonical file owns (a) re-verifying the date and time against an SPF-specific release page rather than the shared calendar row, exactly as the PIES lane did for its own event, (b) deciding whether LOW is right — the proposer's lane deliberately did not re-tier an event it does not own, and an argument exists that a national consensus release deserves medium, and (c) establishing whether the SPF's published forecasts have ever moved a tape, which this sweep did not test. This is a PROPOSAL and an ESTIMATE — it widens caution, licenses nothing, and the proposing ledger registers no forward test that depends on it.
